source_review.notes: Checked ACM, Elsevier, SIAM, Berkeley, institutional, author, official proceedings, and current survey records for Tarjan DSU, Sleator-Tarjan dynamic trees, Henzinger-King randomized connectivity, Holm-de Lichtenberg-Thorup deterministic connectivity, Eppstein et al. sparsification, Patrascu-Demaine lower bounds, Eppstein offline dynamic graph algorithms, and Hanauer-Henzinger-Schulz's 2022 quick reference. Corrected the survey article number to 1.11 against institutional metadata. No latest-best-bound, library-default, product-performance, or universal implementation claim is made.

Checked undirected, stable-universe, total-operation-order, online/offline, deterministic/randomized, worst-case/amortized, and cell-probe qualifiers plus balanced GitHub math delimiters.

evidence: Recomputed every active interval, query result, rollback transition, complexity translation, parallel-edge case, reverse-time example, forest replacement, and version race in the chapter.
Checked 2,207,920 interval-leaf membership cases, 384 graph-version connectivity queries, two multigraph queries, and the log2(2^20)=20 height calculation.

evidence: Re-derived union-by-size logarithmic height, canonical interval coverage, root-to-leaf active-edge equality, rollback restoration, and total offline time and space bounds.
Re-derived the forest insertion, non-tree deletion, tree-edge cut, crossing replacement, and no-replacement disconnection cases.

evidence: Checked empty graphs and traces, isolated vertices, self-loops, one-edge intervals, endpoint boundaries, parallel edges, redundant unions, bridges, cycles, dense cuts, and all 64 simple graphs on four labeled vertices.

Checked unknown and repeated edge IDs, path-compression leakage, missing size restoration, adversarial replacement churn, huge histories, query/update races, log gaps, resharding, unsupported upgrades, and fail-safe recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Directed reachability and dynamic shortest paths are explicitly deferred to ALGE-079 rather than smuggled into undirected connectivity.

evidence: Checked active-edge lifetime, forest acyclicity and spanning, edge classification, replacement crossing, rollback parent/size restoration, branch isolation, metadata, snapshot version, and persistence invariants.

Exhaustive interval decomposition and a Gray-code trace visiting every four-vertex simple graph matched an independent BFS oracle at every pair query; seven rollback union prefixes restored exact baseline state.

evidence: Reviewed intervalization, canonical coverage, traversal induction, DSU correspondence, mutation-log reversal, and complexity accounting as separate proof layers.
Reviewed the online spanning-forest proof and isolated replacement search as the critical algorithmic obligation not supplied by a dynamic tree alone.
proof_review.notes: The executable proves observed bounded behavior only; HLT, Henzinger-King, sparsification, dynamic-tree, and cell-probe theorems are cited rather than re-created.

evidence: Audited proof, induction, invariant, exact, amortized, expected, worst-case, polylogarithmic, lower-bound, offline, online, model, oracle, and operational language.
Separated abstract graph semantics, data-structure representation, complete algorithms, reductions, executable reference, empirical resource judgment, and consistency policy.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No adjacency scan, rollback implementation, or dynamic forest primitive is said to inherit another complete algorithm's asymptotic theorem.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet exited zero with exact versioned connectivity answers for five queries on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution supports the offline implementation and enumerated domains only; it does not establish concurrent correctness, online polylogarithmic performance, production durability, complete log coverage, security, or policy fitness.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed dynamic graph models, deletion impossibility for partition-only DSU, intervalization, segment-tree rollback, online spanning forests, replacement search, dynamic trees, sparsification, upper and lower bounds, and selection trade-offs.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed edge identity, multigraphs, temporal order, concurrency, path witnesses, logs, snapshots, replay, rebuilds, burst workloads, memory estimates, observability, adversarial churn, authorization misuse, and fail-safe fallback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives and executes a complete offline algorithm, explains why online deletion is harder, maps classic advanced results without overclaiming, supplies ten distinct examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, dynamic-graph, database, distributed-systems, platform, security, authorization, performance, or operational review is claimed. Formal guarantees remain limited to their declared graph, update, sequence, model, randomization, amortization, word, space, and output assumptions; production conclusions remain conditional on identity, ordering, persistence, concurrency, workload, adversary, resource, recovery, and downstream-decision conditions.
